indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.4.2.1 Demonstrate knowledge of generation of electricity, its transmission and transformation into other forms
indicator.objective: Identify the symbols used in representing various components in a given circuit diagram

skills.description: Recognise the symbols for battery, switch, bulb, connecting wire, and other components.
Match a symbol to its correct component name.
Draw a simple circuit diagram using correct symbols for battery, switch, and bulb.
Classify materials as conductors, semi-conductors and insulators based on their ability to carry electricity.
Explain why electrical wires are coated with plastic (insulation).
Describe how to test materials using an open circuit to see if they conduct electricity.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Symbols are the same as real components.
The plastic coating on wires carries electricity.
Semi-conductors are the same as insulators.
A bulb can be used to test conductivity without a battery.

questions.stem: In a circuit diagram, what does a long line and a short line side by side represent?
hints: It has a positive and a negative end.
questions.explanation: A long line and a short line side by side represent a battery (or cell) in a circuit diagram.
questions.misconception: Symbols are the same as real components.

questions.stem: In a circuit diagram, what does a circle with a cross inside represent?
questions.explanation: A circle with a cross inside represents a bulb in a circuit diagram.
questions.misconception: A circle with a cross is a battery.

questions.stem: What component does a circle with a cross inside represent in a circuit diagram?
hints: It is a common circuit component.
questions.explanation: A circle with a cross inside represents a bulb.

questions.stem: In a circuit diagram, what does a line with a gap and a small angled line represent?
hints: It can be open or closed.
It controls the flow of electricity.
questions.explanation: A line with a gap and a small angled line represents a switch in a circuit diagram.

questions.stem: Which component matches the symbol of two parallel lines (one long, one short)?
hints: It has positive and negative terminals.
questions.explanation: Two parallel lines (one long, one short) represent a battery.

questions.stem: Which component is represented by a straight line in a circuit diagram?
questions.explanation: A straight line in a circuit diagram represents a connecting wire.
questions.misconception: A straight line represents a battery.

questions.stem: Which set correctly matches symbols to their components?
options: Long and short line → battery; circle with cross → bulb; line with gap → switch
Long and short line → bulb; circle with cross → battery; line with gap → wire
Long and short line → switch; circle with cross → wire; line with gap → bulb
Long and short line → wire; circle with cross → switch; line with gap → battery
hints: Bulb symbol is a circle with a cross.
questions.explanation: The correct matching is: battery → long and short line; bulb → circle with cross; switch → line with gap.

questions.stem: A pupil sees a circle with a cross in a circuit diagram. Which component should be connected there?
questions.explanation: The circle with a cross represents a bulb, so a bulb should be connected there.
questions.misconception: A battery should be connected at the bulb symbol.

questions.stem: What is a conductor?
options: A material that allows electricity to pass through it
questions.explanation: A conductor is a material that allows electricity to pass through it.

questions.stem: What is an insulator?
options: A material that does not allow electricity to pass through it
A material that allows electricity to pass through
questions.explanation: An insulator is a material that does not allow electricity to pass through it.

questions.stem: Is a metal spoon a conductor or an insulator?
questions.explanation: A metal spoon is a conductor because it allows electricity to pass through it.

questions.stem: Which set contains only insulators?
options: Plastic ruler, glass rod, piece of wood
Metal spoon, copper wire, iron nail
Copper wire, plastic ruler, iron nail
hints: Plastic, glass and wood are insulators.
questions.explanation: Plastic, glass and wood are insulators. They do not allow electricity to pass through them.

questions.stem: Why are electrical wires coated with plastic?
options: To insulate the wire and prevent electric shock
questions.explanation: Electrical wires are coated with plastic to insulate them and prevent electric shock.

questions.stem: Why is plastic used to cover electrical wires?
answer: because it is an insulator and prevents electric shock
plastic is an insulator so it stops electricity from escaping
it insulates the wire and protects people
questions.explanation: Plastic is used to cover electrical wires because it is an insulator, which prevents electric shock and keeps electricity inside the wire.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'The plastic coating on a wire helps electricity flow.' What is the best correction?
options: No, plastic is an insulator that stops electricity from flowing out and prevents shock
No, plastic makes the wire heavier
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator. It does not help electricity flow; it stops electricity from flowing out of the wire and protects people from shock.

questions.stem: How can you test whether a material is a conductor or an insulator?
options: Place it in a simple circuit with a battery and bulb; if the bulb lights, it is a conductor
Place it in water and see if it floats
Heat it and see if it melts
hints: Use a circuit with a battery and bulb.
If the bulb lights, electricity flows.
questions.explanation: To test whether a material is a conductor or insulator, place it in a simple circuit with a battery and bulb. If the bulb lights, the material is a conductor.
questions.misconception: A bulb can test conductivity without a battery.

questions.stem: Describe how you would test a material to see if it conducts electricity.
answer: set up a simple circuit with a battery and bulb and place the material in the circuit; if the bulb lights it is a conductor
use a circuit with a battery and bulb and put the material in the gap; if the bulb lights it conducts
connect the material into an open circuit; if the bulb lights, it conducts electricity
questions.explanation: Set up a simple circuit with a battery and bulb. Place the material in the circuit (in the gap). If the bulb lights, the material is a conductor; if it does not, it is an insulator.
questions.misconception: You can test conductivity without a circuit.

criteria.description: Used the correct symbol for a battery
Used the correct symbol for a switch
Used the correct symbol for a bulb
Connected the symbols in a complete loop

questions.stem: Draw a circuit diagram using symbols for a battery, a switch and a bulb. Show the switch in the closed position so the bulb would light.

criteria.description: Used the correct symbol for a battery
Used the correct symbol for a switch
Used the correct symbol for a bulb
Drew the switch in the closed position
The circuit forms a complete loop

criteria.description: Used correct symbols for battery, bulb and switch in both diagrams
Drew the switch in the open position in the first diagram
Drew the switch in the closed position in the second diagram
